name: k-switch
description: Roadmap #10: the k-switch, executed — order superposition over k! topological sorts (k=3 six orders, k=4 twenty-four), the machine-verified layer of the N-switch query separation. Known in theory (ARA14: O(n) vs O(n²) queries), never machine-verified. v0.1.0: the 3-switch as an executable isometry with certificate; the commuting-vs-anticommuting promise read out deterministically via the exact parity-orthogonality law (dimension-free); structural blindness of plain fixed orders; the three-stage scheduling contact surface (six-order switch vs six fixed orders). v0.2.0, the k=4 faces: the parity law survives k=4 (12 even - 12 odd = 0 exactly, sign law exact on all 24 orders); the TCA+21 Hadamard promise at d=2 executed (census of all 256 Pauli gate sets, 136 satisfying, Algorithm 1 reads the column with probability exactly 1); the fixed-order supersequence bound machine-decided (9 uses, 104 minimal witnesses); the exact 24x6 plain-order distinguishability matrix (all zeros — no plain order separates any column pair); the d=4 Pauli census (0 commuting quadruples — an honest no-go, 30 anticommuting; matched blindness pairs only outside the Pauli universe, constructed and verified); and the 24-order scheduling contact surface (fixed orders 1/sqrt2 survives, the halving law breaks: switch D = sqrt(10)/6). v0.3.0, the quality wave: type hardening, a named error surface (every public throw coded, illegal inputs named and rejected), kernel single-sourcing, dead-code settlement — mathematics frozen, every report bit-identical
